Greece
grēs
n. (the land of the Hellenes; in prophecy, the third of Daniel's four kingdoms; the AV also has Grecia)
Latin Graecia. The AV uses Grecia in Daniel and Zechariah and Greece in Acts, and calls its people Greeks or Grecians — the latter often for Greek-speaking Jews.

Biblical Definition

Greece is the Hellenic world. Paul travelled there: “when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece” (Act 20:2), and at Athens “his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry” (Act 17:16). Daniel names it in prophecy before its rise: “the rough goat is the king of Grecia” (Dan 8:21). Zechariah sets Zion against it: “and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece” (Zec 9:13). And Greeks come looking for Christ at the last Passover: “Sir, we would see Jesus” (John 12:20–21).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines Grecian as pertaining to Greece; and Greek as a native of Greece, or the language of Greece, which is one of the most perfect of languages.

GRECIAN, a. Pertaining to Greece.

GRECIAN, n. A native of Greece; also, a Jew who understood Greek; and a scholar versed in the Greek language.

GREEK, n. A native of Greece.

2. The language of Greece.

Key Scripture

Act 20:2 — "And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,"

Act 17:16 — "Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry."

Dan 8:21 — "And the rough goat is the king of Grecia: and the great horn that is between his eyes is the first king."

Zec 9:13 — "When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece, and made thee as the sword of a mighty man."

John 12:20 — "And there were certain Greeks among them that came up to worship at the feast:"

Modern Corruption

Greece is treated as the church's cultural enemy or as its philosophical foundation, and the New Testament used its language while refusing its wisdom.

expand to see more

The providence is worth stating plainly because it cuts against both simple positions. Alexander's conquests gave the Mediterranean world a common tongue; three centuries later the apostles wrote the New Testament in it, and the Old Testament had already been translated into it at Alexandria. The gospel travelled on Greek roads, in Greek, to cities Greek colonists had built. A Christian who despises Greece has to explain why the Spirit chose its language, and why Paul quoted its poets on Mars' hill.

The other reading goes too far the other way, treating Athens as a preparation the gospel merely completed. First Corinthians 1 forecloses that: the Greeks seek after wisdom, and Christ crucified is unto the Greeks foolishness. Paul is not saying they lacked information; he is saying the cross does not fit inside the category of wisdom they had built, and cannot be made to. Acts 17 ends with the sermon breaking on exactly that point — when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked.

Acts 17:16 gives the personal note that keeps the subject from being an abstraction. Paul walks into the most beautiful city in the ancient world, and his spirit is stirred in him — provoked, exasperated — because he saw it wholly given to idolatry. He did not see the architecture first. Then in John 12 the movement runs the other way: Greeks come up to the feast and ask Philip, Sir, we would see Jesus — and the Lord answers that the hour is come that the Son of man should be glorified, and speaks of a corn of wheat falling into the ground and dying. The Greeks got their answer, and it was the cross.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek Hellas (G1671), Greece; Hellen (G1672), a Greek; Hellenistes (G1675), a Grecian, Greek-speaking Jew; Hebrew Yavan (H3120), Javan, Greece.

expand to see more

Greek Hellas (G1671) — Greece; Acts 20:2 only.

Greek Hellen (G1672) — a Greek, a Gentile; John 12:20, Romans 1:16, 1 Corinthians 1:22–24, Galatians 3:28.

Hebrew Yavan (H3120) — Javan, Greece; Daniel 8:21, 10:20, Zechariah 9:13, Genesis 10:2.

Usage

"“The rough goat is the king of Grecia” — named before it rose."

"“His spirit was stirred in him” — he did not see the architecture first."

"“Sir, we would see Jesus” — and the answer was a corn of wheat, and the cross."
